items.title: The Invisible Lottery: How Subtle Cues Steer Algorithm Choice in LLM Code Generation
items.quote: We define algorithm steering as cue-induced shifts in algorithm-family distributions and run 46,535 controlled experiments across 11 tasks
items.relation: behavioural default-algorithm steering by incidental cues under fixed correctness; no literal multi-name bans, no activation geometry

items.title: Benchmarking Language Model Creativity: A Case Study on Code Generation (NeoCoder, NAACL 2025)
items.quote: We introduce DENIAL PROMPTING which pushes LLMs to develop more creative solutions to a given prob
items.relation: technique-level bans (denial prompting) to elicit creative code; behavioural only, frontier models, no per-model mechanism labels or manifold landing

items.title: Manifold Steering Reveals the Shared Geometry of Neural Network Representation and Behavior
items.quote: we test whether interventions that respect the geometry of activation space will yield behaviors close to those the model exhibits naturally
items.relation: activation-manifold vs behaviour-manifold link via interventions; our landing test is correlational and uses prohibition, not steering

items.title: Language Models Represent and Transform Concepts with Shared Geometry
items.quote: Across six model families of varying scales, we find that context moves each concept differently.
items.relation: context-induced displacement of concept point-cloud manifolds; not algorithm choice under bans

items.title: AlgoTrace: Algorithmic Primitives and Compositional Geometry of Reasoning in Language Models (ICML 2026)
items.quote: We operationalize primitives by clustering latent activations of the model when solving four benchmarks: Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), 3SAT, AIME, and Graph Navigation.
items.relation: geometry of algorithmic primitives inside reasoning traces; no catalogue of named path-search algorithms, no ban/landing test

items.title: Beyond Linear Concepts: Discovering and Aligning Non-Linear Concept Manifolds in Large Language Models
items.relation: method for non-linear concept manifolds; no behavioural prohibition

items.title: Formalize, Don't Optimize: The Heuristic Trap in LLM-Generated Combinatorial Solvers
items.quote: evaluate three solver-construction paradigms: native algorithmic search (Python), constraint modeling through a Python solver API (Python + OR-Tools), and declarative constraint mod
items.relation: solver-synthesis paradigms for combinatorial problems; no algorithm bans or default-choice study

positioning.overall: No retrieved work occupies the combination tested here (a multi-model screen of a literal five-name algorithm ban with mechanism-level labels, plus survivor landing on an activation manifold of the algorithm catalogue). Behavioural neighbours (Invisible Lottery, NeoCoder denial prompting) and geometry neighbours (Manifold Steering, shared concept geometry, AlgoTrace) are adjacent.

deviations.text: The GPU is an NVIDIA RTX 2000 Ada (16 GB), not the planned RTX A4500 (20 GB), and the container has no C compiler (vLLM runs eager, no CUDA graphs / torch.compile). Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B cannot be served in bf16 by vLLM on 16 GB; see D9.

Provider heterogeneity: OpenRouter configurations run at provider precision (DeepInfra fp8 for Qwen3-14B/32B and gemma-3-27b, Cloudflare unknown for Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, CoreWeave bf16 for Llama-3.1-8B), pinned with allow_fallbacks false; no CRN coupling; every table and figure carries the engine tag.

Qwen3-8B thinking-on (C1) is sampled with the official FP8 checkpoint in vLLM 0.11.0 (W8A16 Marlin, eager), N_base = 30 (baseline known collapsed: art_UoCVh2Qe5RZ0 800/800 BFS); its geometry (if needed) is bf16.

Geometry on a quantised model (int8/nf4) departs from 'never quantise a model that carries a claim'; the quantisation check (bf16 vs int8 vs nf4 on Qwen3-8B, state cosines + Spearman of 10x10 geodesic matrices) runs whenever the selected model is quantised; < 0.8 -> PRECISION-SENSITIVE.

Algorithm-level exact permutation null (120 permutations of algorithm identities, count profile fixed) is quoted beside the committed per-program nulls; its floor is 0.2 (1/5) when one algorithm takes every survivor: one model and one landing algorithm cannot reach algorithm-level significance.
Correctness filter confound: a can-weighted null C (correct-when-forced rates, +0.5 smoothed) and an attempted-survivor variant (no pass filter) are reported.

The 10-class labeller failed its gold gate for dijkstra_unit, JPS and bidirectional A* (iteration 2): every program that decides the screen is adjudicated (correct candidate survivors, 'other', those 3 classes, plus a 10% audit of in-banned labels); the adjudicated column is primary.

Thinking budgets differ: local C1 = two-phase forced close at 8,192 thinking tokens; OpenRouter thinking configurations are bounded by max_tokens 9,728 and truncate; per-configuration truncation rates reported.
Hardware: RTX 2000 Ada 16 GB (not A4500 20 GB), no C compiler (vLLM eager, no CUDA graphs).

C2 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is sampled through OpenRouter (CoreWeave bf16, pinned) instead of local vLLM bf16: bf16 8B weights (16.1 GB) do not fit a 16 GB GPU under vLLM; the GPU is reserved for C1 and the geometry.

DeepInfra ignores reasoning {enabled:false} for Qwen3 (smoke: ~1,600 reasoning tokens, truncation); the Qwen3 soft switch ' /no_think' is appended to the user turn of C3 and C5 only (smoke2: reasoning 1 token).

C7 planned google/gemma-3-12b-it (DeepInfra bf16): endpoints returned 504 after 300 s (2/3 first attempts) and no other bf16/fp8 provider exists -> same-family substitute google/gemma-3-27b-it (DeepInfra fp8), chosen before commit #1 over the plan's first substitute (qwen3-30b-a3b) to keep a new Gemma-family row; states (if selected) from unsloth/gemma-3-27b-it-bnb-4bit (nf4).

Judge gate: google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite scored 7/10 (failed); adjudication pair = deepseek-chat-v3.1 (9/10) + kimi-k2 (10/10); third judge = mistral-medium-3.1 (9/10); the labeller's disagreement judge is deepseek-chat-v3.1 (iteration 2 used gpt-4.1-mini).
OpenRouter seed = slot index + 1 (Cloudflare rejects seed 0); local vLLM seed = slot index.
Primary hidden suite (ITER2 exp9 tests.json) holds 48 cases (the plan text says 45); all 15 T1 references (the plan's '25' counts T1 + T2) pass all 48 and the 41-case ITER1 exp2 suite.
C1 projected time 76 min for 30 + 50 rows (> 45 min; measured 57.2 s/row on the 16 GB card) -> N_ban cut to the committed floor 30 (W1/W2/W3 10/10/10)
M2 for C6 (thinking, 32.8B at nf4): reasoning capped at the first 4,096 tokens (plan fallback g-iii) and baseline programs limited to a seeded sample of 30 (plan TIME rule); every ban program is kept

Decisive 'other' survivors whose agreed judge label names a BFS/DFS variant (C6 confirmation rows 6/12/18 and others) were read by the executor (results/executor_review.json). The committed adjudication stays primary; strict sensitivities (drop BFS/DFS-variant and SPFA 'other' survivors) are reported: C6 screen 0.34 -> 0.22, confirmation 0.42 -> 0.28, both still >= 0.20; catalogue-only 0.12 / 0.18.

The first quantisation-check run stopped at the embedding identity check (accelerate keeps CPU-placed weights as meta tensors); the bf16 states were kept, the record was rebuilt, and the embedding identity was re-tested separately (T7: CPU-embedding vs all-GPU block outputs identical).

Novelty audit: Zhang-Shasha distances are computed for the top 3 corpus programs by AST node-histogram cosine (size-matched, <= 1,200 nodes) to keep the pure-Python tree edit distance tractable; candidates run in 5 spawn workers.

prompt_rules.ban: cap_first(W with {X} = display names of B joined 'A, B, C, D or E' in canonical order rotated by W_ROT) + blank line + SPEC

bibfs: a breadth-first search run from both start and goal
astar: A* search with a Manhattan-distance heuristic
gbfs: greedy best-first search with a Manhattan heuristic
dijkstra_unit: Dijkstra's algorithm with unit edge weights
jps: jump point search (JPS) on a uniform-cost grid
biastar: A* run from both start and goal at once

prompt_rules.forced: cap_first(forced_templates[t] with {X} = alias_j(a)) + blank line + SPEC; 10 x 3 = 30 per algorithm; group = (t, j)

commit1.banned_set_rule: B_c = 5 largest implemented counts in c's baseline (adjudicated label; pass or fail; 'invalid' and 'other' excluded); ties -> higher correct count, then canonical order; if < 5 classes have count >= 1, fill from [bfs, dfs, gbfs, iddfs, astar] in that order
commit1.labeller: last ```python fence of the answer (no fence = invalid) -> 48-case ITER2 exp9 suite (primary) + 41-case ITER1 exp2 suite (secondary) -> exp9 labeller_ext runtime + AST rules -> deepseek-chat-v3.1 on disagreement -> exp9 combine = label_raw
commit1.adjudication: A = ban rows that pass with label_raw not in B_c + every row labelled other/dijkstra_unit/jps/biastar (baseline rows before commit #2) + stratified random 10% of in-banned ban rows (audit, seed 0); two gated judges (deepseek-chat-v3.1, kimi-k2), blind to configuration and arm; agree -> adj_label; disagree -> third judge mistral-medium-3.1 + executor manual read decide (logged); audit disagreement > 10% for a configuration -> all its ban rows adjudicated
commit1.screen_metrics: correct_survivor = passed and adj_label not in B_c and adj_label in catalogue or known-outside (other resolved to a named known algorithm); share_cs with Wilson 95%; attempted_survivor; banned_mechanism; name_free_reimpl (code; code+answer+reasoning) by alias regex; pass, invalid, truncation; per-template table; baseline-to-ban composition shifts with Newcombe intervals

selection.rule: Q = {c: share_cs >= 0.20}; m* = argmax share_cs; ties within 0.02 -> higher Wilson lower bound, then fewer parameters, then local; Q empty -> TP_RESULT = 'no tested open model obeys a five-name ban on this task' with every share and one-sided 95% upper bound; geometry DESCRIPTIVE on the configuration with the most correct survivors (C1 = Qwen3-8B bf16 if all 0); no confirmation

geometry.summary: S-mean = mean of block outputs over tokens whose char offsets lie inside SPEC (rendered chat text, offset mapping)
geometry.layer: L* = argmax over blocks of grouped 10-fold CV balanced accuracy (groups = (t, j); standardise, PCA(64) in fold, multinomial LR C=1.0); ties within 0.01 -> block nearest depth 0.5; all at ceiling -> block nearest depth 0.5 among ceiling blocks; forced prompts only (outcome-blind)
geometry.manifold: raw float64 coordinates at L*: PCA 2D (EVR), classical MDS on 300 points and 10 centroids with Kruskal stress-1, Isomap k in {5,10,15} on the symmetrised kNN distance graph with shortest inter-component edges added if disconnected (component count recorded), geodesics by scipy shortest_path
geometry.g: g_k(a) = min over b in B of mean geodesic distance over pairs (points of a, points of b) (iteration-7 top5geo.py definition); med = median of g over the 5 non-banned; EDGE g < med, MIDDLE g == med, OPPOSITE g > med; Euclidean-centroid variant
geometry.reliability: split-half Spearman of 10x10 mean-geodesic matrices (groups 0-14 vs 15-29); 1,000 bootstrap resamples of paraphrase groups -> class and nearest-banned stability

landing.surv: correct ban rows of m* whose adj_label is one of the 5 non-banned catalogue algorithms; n_s < 5 -> DESCRIPTIVE ONLY
landing.statistic: S = mean over Surv of g_k(label) at (L*, k=10; if disconnected the smallest connected k)

nulls.U: iid uniform over the 5 non-banned, 10,000 draws, seed 0 (committed)
nulls.F: iid by m*'s baseline frequency among non-banned +0.5 smoothing, 10,000 draws (committed; near-uniform flag if all counts 0)

Please solve the following programming task.

Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal) that finds a path between two cells of a grid. grid is a list of equal-length strings with between 1 and 30 rows and between 1 and 30 columns; the character . is a free cell and the character # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of 0-based indices. A move goes to one of the 4 orthogonal neighbours (up, down, left, right) and may not leave the grid or enter a wall. Return a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal, and in which consecutive cells are neighbours and every cell is free. Any valid path is accepted; it does not have to be the shortest. If start equals goal and the cell is free, return [start]. If no path exists, or start or goal is a wall, return [].

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    start_row, start_col = start
    goal_row, goal_col = goal
    if grid[start_row][start_col] == '#' or grid[goal_row][goal_col] == '#':
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    from collections import deque
    queue = deque()
    queue.append([start])
    visited = set()
    visited.add(start)
    while queue:
        current_path = queue.popleft()
        current_pos = current_path[-1]
        if current_pos == (goal_row, goal_col):
            return current_path
        for dr, dc in directions:
            new_row = current_pos[0] + dr
            new_col = current_pos[1] + dc
            if 0 <= new_row < rows and 0 <= new_col < cols:
                new_pos = (new_row, new_col)
                if grid[new_row][new_col] == '.' and new_pos not in visited:
                    visited.add(new_pos)
                    new_path = current_path + [new_pos]
                    queue.append(new_path)
    return []
```

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    visited = [[False]*cols for _ in range(rows)]
    current_path = [[False]*(cols+2) for _ in range(rows+2)]
    queue = deque([start])
    current_path[start[0]][start[1]] = True
    directions = [(0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)]
    
    while queue:
        row, col = queue.popleft()
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path = []
            while (row, col) != start:
                path.append((row, col))
                prev_row, prev_col = row-1 if col < cols-1 else row, col-1
                current_path[prev_row][prev_col] = False
                row, col = prev_row, prev_col
            path.append(start)
            return path[::-1]
        
        for dr, dc in directions:
            new_row, new_col = row+dr, col+dc
            if (1 <= new_row < rows and 1 <= new_col < cols and 
                grid[new_row-1][new_col-1] == '.' and not visited[new_row-1][new_col-1]):
                queue.append((new_row, new_col))
                visited[new_row-1][new_col-1] = True
                current_path[new_row-1][new_col-1] = True
                
    return []
```

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    x, y = start
    queue = deque([(x, y, [start])]
    visited = set([start])
    
    directions = [(0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)]
    
    while queue:
        (cx, cy, path) = queue.popleft()

                queue.append(((vx, vy), new_path))
                visited.add((vx, vy))
                
    return []
```

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
```

```python
from random import shuffle

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    n_rows = len(grid)
    n_cols = len(grid[0])
    directions = [(0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)]
    queue = [(start, [start])]
    good_positions = [(r, c) for r in range(n_rows) for c in range(n_cols) if grid[r][c] == '.']

    while queue:
        (x, path) = queue.pop()
        a, b = neighbors((n_rows, n_cols), x)
        shuffle(a)
        shuffle(b)
        r_answer = [x]
        for(dx, dy) in zip(a, b):

            if (nx, ny) == goal:

            elif (nx, ny) in good_positions:
                r_answer = [i for i in r_answer + [(nx, ny)] if i in good_positions]
                queue.insert(0, ((nx, ny), r_answer))

    return []

def neighbors(size, position):
    (r, c) = position
    n_rows, _ = size
    return [(r0, c) for r0 in [r-1, r+1] if 0 <= r0 < n_rows] + [(r, c0) for c0 in [c-1, c+1] if 0 <= c < size[1]]
```

```python
                new_path = path + [(new_r, new_c)]
                queue.append(new_path)
    return []
```

```python
    if (start == goal and grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.') or (start == goal and grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#'):
        return [start] if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.' else []

    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0
```

```python
        from collections import deque
        queue = deque()
```

```python
        visited.add(start)

            current = queue.popleft()

        return False

    if bfs():
        current = goal
        path.append(current)
```

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])
    s_row, s_col = start
    g_row, g_col = goal
    # Check if start is valid
    if s_row < 0 or s_row >= rows or s_col < 0 or s_col >= cols:
        return []
    if grid[s_row][s_col] == '#':
        return []
    # Check if goal is valid
    if g_row < 0 or g_row >= rows or g_col < 0 or g_col >= cols:
        return []
    if grid[g_row][g_col] == '#':
        return []
    # Check if start is goal
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    # Now perform BFS
    visited = set()
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((s_row, s_col))
    visited.add((s_row, s_col))
    parent = {}
    found = False
    while queue:
        r, c = queue.popleft()
        # Check all four directions
        for dr, dc in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]:
            nr = r + dr
            nc = c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if (nr, nc) not in visited and grid[nr][nc] == '.':
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    parent[(nr, nc)] = (r, c)
                    queue.append((nr, nc))
                    if (nr, nc) == (g_row, g_col):
                        found = True
                        break
        if found:
            break
    if not found:
        return []
    # Reconstruct path
    path = []
    current = (g_row, g_col)
    while current is not None:
        path.append(current)
        current = parent.get(current, None)
    path.reverse()
    return path
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])
    # Check if start and goal are within the grid boundaries
    if (start[0] < 0 or start[0] >= rows or start[1] < 0 or start[1] >= cols or
        goal[0] < 0 or goal[0] >= rows or goal[1] < 0 or goal[1] >= cols):
        return []
    # Check if start or goal is a wall
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    from collections import deque
    queue = deque([start])
    visited = {start}
    parent = {}
    found = False
    # Directions: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    while queue:
        current = queue.popleft()
        if current == goal:
            found = True
            break
        for dr, dc in directions:
            new_r = current[0] + dr
            new_c = current[1] + dc
            if 0 <= new_r < rows and 0 <= new_c < cols:
                if (new_r, new_c) not in visited and grid[new_r][new_c] == '.':
                    visited.add((new_r, new_c))
                    parent[(new_r, new_c)] = current
                    queue.append((new_r, new_c))
    if not found:
        return []
    # Reconstruct the path
    path = []
    current = goal
    while current is not None:
        path.append(current)
        current = parent.get(current, None)
    path.reverse()
    return path
```

    cols = len(grid[0])

Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal) that finds a path between two cells of a grid. grid is a list of equal-length strings with between 1 and 30 rows and between 1 and 30 columns; the character . is a free cell and the character # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of 0-based indices. A move goes to one of the 4 orthogonal neighbours (up, down, left, right) and may not leave the grid or enter a wall. Return a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal, and in which consecutive cells are neighbours and every cell is free. Any valid path is accepted; it does not have to be the shortest. If start equals goal and the cell is free, return [start]. If no path exists, or start or goal is a wall, return [].

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Check if start or goal is a wall or out of bounds
    if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols and grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.'):
        return []
    if not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols and grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '.'):
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    
    # Directions: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    # BFS to find a path
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((start, [start]))
    visited = set([start])
    
    while queue:
        (current, path) = queue.popleft()
        for dr, dc in directions:
            r, c = current[0] + dr, current[1] + dc
            if (0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols and
                grid[r][c] == '.' and (r, c) not in visited):
                if (r, c) == goal:
                    return path + [(r, c)]
                queue.append(( (r, c), path + [(r, c)] ))
                visited.add( (r, c) )
    
    return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])

        return []

    parent = [[None for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]

        for dr, dc in directions:
```

```python
            if is_valid(nr, nc):
                visited[nr][nc] = True
                parent[(nr, nc)] = curr
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    from collections import deque
    
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    def is_valid(r, c):
        return 0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols and grid[r][c] == '.'
    
    visited = [[False for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]
    prev = [[None for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]
    queue = deque()
    
    sr, sc = start
    gr, gc = goal
    
    if not (is_valid(sr, sc) and is_valid(gr, gc)):
        return []
    
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    
    queue.append((sr, sc))
    visited[sr][sc] = True
    
    while queue:
        r, c = queue.popleft()
        for dr, dc in [(-1,0), (1,0), (0,-1), (0,1)]:
            new_r, new_c = r + dr, c + dc
            if is_valid(new_r, new_c) and not visited[new_r][new_c]:
                visited[new_r][new_c] = True
                prev[new_r][new_c] = (r, c)
                queue.append((new_r, new_c))
                if (new_r, new_c) == goal:
                    path = []
                    curr = goal
                    while curr:
                        path.append(curr)
                        curr = prev[curr[0]][curr[1]]
                    return path[::-1]
    
    return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0

    if (
        not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols) or
        not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols)
    ):
        return []

    start_char = grid[start[0]][start[1]]
    goal_char = grid[goal[0]][goal[1]]
    if start_char == '#' or goal_char == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    visited = set()
    stack = [(start, [start])]

    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    while stack:

        if (r, c) == goal:
            return path

        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if (
                0 <= nr < rows and
                0 <= nc < cols and
                grid[nr][nc] == '.' and
                (nr, nc) not in visited
            ):
                visited.add((nr, nc))
                stack.append(((nr, nc), path + [(nr, nc))))
    return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    from collections import deque

    def is_valid(pos):
        r, c = pos
        return 0 <= r < len(grid) and 0 <= c < len(grid[0]) and grid[r][c] == '.'

                visited.add(next_pos)
                queue.append((next_pos, path + [next_pos]))
    return []
```

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if not grid or not grid[0]:
        return []
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    if (start[0] < 0 or start[0] >= rows or start[1] < 0 or start[1] >= cols or
        goal[0] < 0 or goal[0] >= rows or goal[1] < 0 or goal[1] >= cols):
        return []
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    visited = set()
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((start, [start]))
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    while queue:
        (row, col), path = queue.popleft()
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = row + dr, col + dc
            if (0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and
                grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited):
                new_path = path + [(nr, nc)]
                if (nr, nc) == goal:
                    return new_path
                visited.add((nr, nc))
                queue.append(((nr, nc), new_path))
    return []
```

Here's a concise and well-structured solution to the problem using Breadth-First Search (BFS) to find a path between two cells in a grid. The implementation includes necessary checks for valid input and uses a parent mapping to reconstruct the path from the destination back to the starting point.

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])

    def is_valid(r, c):
        return 0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols

    start_r, start_c = start
    goal_r, goal_c = goal

    # Check if start or goal is invalid (out of bounds or wall)
    if not is_valid(start_r, start_c) or not is_valid(goal_r, goal_c):
        return []

    if grid[start_r][start_c] == '#' or grid[goal_r][goal_c] == '#':
        return []

    # If start is the same as goal, return a single-element list
    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    from collections import deque
    queue = deque()
    visited = set()
    parent = {}

    queue.append(start)
    visited.add(start)

    found = False

    while queue:
        current = queue.popleft()
        if current == goal:
            found = True
            break

        # Explore all 4 orthogonal neighbors
        directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
        for dr, dc in directions:
            new_r = current[0] + dr
            new_c = current[1] + dc
            neighbor = (new_r, new_c)

            if is_valid(new_r, new_c) and grid[new_r][new_c] == '.' and neighbor not in visited:
                visited.add(neighbor)
                queue.append(neighbor)
                parent[neighbor] = current

    # No path was found
    if not found:
        return []

    # Reconstruct the path using the parent map
    path = []
    current = goal
    while current is not None:
        path.append(current)
        current = parent.get(current)
    path.reverse()
    return path
```

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0

    start_r, start_c = start
    goal_r, goal_c = goal

    # Check if start and goal coordinates are valid and not walls
    if not (0 <= start_r < rows and 0 <= start_c < cols):
        return []
    if not (0 <= goal_r < rows and 0 <= goal_c < cols):
        return []
    if grid[start_r][start_c] == '#':
        return []
    if grid[goal_r][goal_c] == '#':
        return []

    # Return immediately if the start and goal are identical and valid
    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    directions = [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1)]
    visited = set()
    parent = {}
    queue = deque()

    queue.append(start)
    visited.add(start)

    found = False

    while queue:
        current = queue.popleft()
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = current[0] + dr, current[1] + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                    if (nr, nc) == (goal_r, goal_c):
                        parent[(nr, nc)] = current
                        found = True
                        queue = deque()  # Clear queue to exit loop
                        break
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    parent[(nr, nc)] = current
                    queue.append((nr, nc))
        if found:
            break

    if not found:
        return []

    # Reconstruct the path from goal to start
    path = []
    current_node = (goal_r, goal_c)
    while current_node is not None:
        path.append(current_node)
        current_node = parent.get(current_node)
    path.reverse()

    return path
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Check if start or goal are valid
    def is_valid(r, c):
        return 0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols and grid[r][c] == '.'
    
    start_r, start_c = start
    goal_r, goal_c = goal
    
    if not is_valid(start_r, start_c) or not is_valid(goal_r, goal_c):
        return []
    
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    
    stack = [(start, [start])]
    visited = set([start])
    
    while stack:
        current, path = stack.pop()
        r, c = current
        
        for dr, dc in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if is_valid(nr, nc) and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                new_path = path + [(nr, nc)]
                new_visited = visited.copy()
                new_visited.add((nr, nc))
                stack.append(((nr, nc), new_path))
                visited = new_visited  # Update visited to avoid same cell in other paths
        
        if path[-1] == (goal_r, goal_c):
            return path
    
    return []
```

To solve the given task of finding a path through a grid, we design an algorithm that avoids all the common search techniques (BFS, DFS, etc.) that are explicitly prohibited. Instead, we use a **priority-based search with randomized priorities**, which offers a randomized, non-deterministic exploration of the path space, and satisfies the problem's constraints.

---

### 🔍 Approach Overview

The algorithm relies on a **priority queue (heapq)**, where the priority of each cell is **randomly assigned**, and the queue is processed by popping the cell with the smallest random priority. This ensures **non-deterministic exploration**, and avoids matching the semantics of standard search algorithms. 

When each cell is explored, its neighbors are added to the queue only if they:
- Have not been visited before
- Are not walls
- Are within bounds

To reconstruct the path once the goal is reached, we maintain a **parent dictionary**, which maps each visited cell to its predecessor along the path.

---

### 🧹 Constraints

This approach:
- Avoids any use of `DFS`, `BFS`, `IDDFS`, `A*`, or `greedy best-first` by design
- Uses only the **standard library** (`heapq`, `random`)
- Handles edge cases like:
  - Start or goal is not a free cell (i.e., `#`)
  - Start is the same as the goal
  - No valid path exists

---

### 🧪 Code

```python
import heapq
import random

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    if not rows:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])

    # Check if start or goal is a wall or out of bounds
    for pos in [start, goal]:
        if not (0 <= pos[0] < rows and 0 <= pos[1] < cols) or grid[pos[0]][pos[1]] == '#':
            return []

    # If start is the same as goal and is a free cell
    if start == goal and grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.':
        return [start]

    # Movement directions: up, right, down, left
    directions = [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1)]

    # Priority queue (priority, (row, col))
    pq = []
    heapq.heappush(pq, (random.random(), start))

    # Parent map for path reconstruction
    parent = {}

    # Visited set to avoid cycles and repeated visits
    visited = set([start])

    while pq:
        current = heapq.heappop(pq)[1]

        if current == goal:
            # Reconstruct path
            path = []
            while current:
                path.append(current)
                current = parent.get(current)
            return path[::-1]

        r, c = current
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            next_cell = (nr, nc)
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and next_cell not in visited:
                    visited.add(next_cell)
                    parent[next_cell] = current
                    heapq.heappush(pq, (random.random(), next_cell))

    return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])
    if (not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols) or
        not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols)):
        return []
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    
    INF = float('inf')
    distance = [[INF] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    pred = [[None] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    sr, sc = start
    distance[sr][sc] = 0
    
    for _ in range(rows * cols - 1):
        updated = False
        for r in range(rows):
            for c in range(cols):
                if grid[r][c] == '#':
                    continue
                current_dist = distance[r][c]
                if current_dist == INF:
                    continue
                for dr, dc in [(-1,0), (1,0), (0,-1), (0,1)]:
                    nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                    if (0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and
                        grid[nr][nc] != '#' and
                        distance[nr][nc] > current_dist + 1):
                        distance[nr][nc] = current_dist + 1
                        pred[nr][nc] = (r, c)
                        updated = True
        if not updated:
            break
    
    gr, gc = goal
    if distance[gr][gc] == INF:
        return []
    
    path = []
    current = goal
    while current is not None:
        path.append(current)
        cr, cc = current
        current = pred[cr][cc]
    path.reverse()
    return path if path[0] == start else []
```

import heapq
import random

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0
    # Check if start equals goal
    if start == goal:
        r, c = start
        if 0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols and grid[r][c] == '.':
            return [start]
        else:
            return []
    # Validate start and goal positions
    sr, sc = start
    gr, gc = goal
    if not (0 <= sr < rows and 0 <= sc < cols and 0 <= gr < rows and 0 <= gc < cols):
        return []
    if grid[sr][sc] == '#' or grid[gr][gc] == '#':
        return []
    # Directions
    directions = [(-1,0), (1,0), (0,-1), (0,1)]
    visited = set()
    heap = []
    parents = {}
    # Initialize
    heapq.heappush(heap, (random.random(), start))
    visited.add(start)
    found = False
    while heap:
        _, current = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if current == goal:
            found = True
            break
        r, c = current
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    parents[(nr, nc)] = current
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (random.random(), (nr, nc)))
    if not found:
        return []
    # Reconstruct path
    path = []
    curr = goal
    while curr != start:
        path.append(curr)
        curr = parents[curr]
    path.append(start)
    return path[::-1]

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if not grid:
        return []
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols and
            0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols):
        return []
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    if start == goal and grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.':
        return [start]

    queue = [(start, [start])]
    visited = {start}

    while queue:
        (row, col), path = queue.pop(0)

        if (row, col) == goal:
            return path

        neighbors = [(row - 1, col), (row + 1, col), (row, col - 1), (row, col + 1)]

        for r, c in neighbors:
            if (0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols and
                    grid[r][c] == '.' and (r, c) not in visited):
                queue.append(((r, c), path + [(r, c)]))
                visited.add((r, c))

    return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if not grid:
        return []
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols and
            0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols):
        return []
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal and grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.':
        return [start]

    queue = [(start, [start])]
    visited = {start}

    while queue:
        (row, col), path = queue.pop(0)

        if (row, col) == goal:
            return path

        neighbors = [(row - 1, col), (row + 1, col), (row, col - 1), (row, col + 1)]

        for nr, nc in neighbors:
            if (0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and
                    grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited):
                queue.append(((nr, nc), path + [(nr, nc)]))
                visited.add((nr, nc))

    return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if not grid:
        return []

    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])

    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= col < cols and grid[row][col] == '.'

    if not is_valid(start[0], start[1]) or not is_valid(goal[0], goal[1]):
        return []

    if start == goal and is_valid(start[0], start[1]):
        return [start]

    visited = set()
    path = []

    def find_path(row, col):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path.append((row, col))
            return True

        if not is_valid(row, col) or (row, col) in visited:
            return False

        visited.add((row, col))
        path.append((row, col))

        # Explore neighbors
        if find_path(row - 1, col):  # Up
            return True
        if find_path(row + 1, col):  # Down
            return True
        if find_path(row, col - 1):  # Left
            return True
        if find_path(row, col + 1):  # Right
            return True

        path.pop()  # Backtrack
        return False

    if find_path(start[0], start[1]):
        return path
    else:
        return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    from queue import Queue
    
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return
    
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    directions = [(0,1), (1, 0), (0,-1), (-1, 0)]
    q = Queue()
    q.put((start, [start]))
    visited = set()
    visited.add(start)
    
    while not q.empty():
        current, path = q.get()
        
        for dr, dc in directions:
            new_row, new_col = current[0] + dr, current[1] + dc
            if 0<= new_row < rows and 0<= new_col < cols and (new_row, new_col) not in visited and grid[new_row][new_col] == '.':
                new_path = path + [(new_row, new_col)]
                if (new_row, new_col) == goal:
                    return new_path
                q.put(((new_row, new_col), new_path))
                visited.add((new_row, new_col))
    
    return []
```

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if start == goal:
        return [start] if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.' else []
    
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0
    
    visited = set()
    prev = {}
    q = deque()
    
    visited.add(start)
    q.append(start)
    
    found = False
    
    while q:
        current = q.popleft()
        current_row, current_col = current
        
        if current == goal:
            found = True
            break
        
        first = True
        for dr, dc in [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1)]:
            nr = current_row + dr
            nc = current_col + dc
            next_node = (nr, nc)

                    prev[next_node] = current
                    if first:

                    else:
                        q.append(next_node)
                    first = False
    
    if not found:
        return []
    
    path = []
    current = goal
    while current != start:
        path.append(current)
        current = prev[current]
    path.append(start)
    path.reverse()
    return path
```

```python
import heapq

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    visited = set()
    heap = []
    heapq.heappush(heap, (start[0] + start[1], start, [start]))
    visited.add(start)
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    while heap:
        _, current, path = heapq.heappop(heap)
        r, c = current
        if current == goal:
            return path
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                next_cell = (nr, nc)
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and next_cell not in visited:
                    visited.add(next_cell)
                    new_path = path + [next_cell]
                    priority = nr + nc
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (priority, next_cell, new_path))
    return []
```

```python
import heapq

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    dist = [[float('inf')] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    dist[start[0]][start[1]] = 0
    heap = []
    heapq.heappush(heap, (0, start[0], start[1]))
    parent = {}
    while heap:
        current_dist, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if (r, c) == goal:
            break
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and dist[nr][nc] == float('inf'):
                    dist[nr][nc] = current_dist + 1
                    parent[(nr, nc)] = (r, c)
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (dist[nr][nc], nr, nc))
    if goal not in parent:
        return []
    path = []
    current = goal
    while current != start:
        path.append(current)
        current = parent[current]
    path.append(start)
    path.reverse()
    return path
```

```python
import heapq

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    directions = [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1)]
    heap = []
    heapq.heappush(heap, (start[0] + start[1], start[0], start[1]))
    visited = set()
    visited.add((start[0], start[1]))
    predecessors = {(start[0], start[1]): None}
    found = False
    while heap:
        priority, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap)
        current = (r, c)
        if current == goal:
            found = True
            break
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    predecessors[(nr, nc)] = current
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (nr + nc, nr, nc))
    if not found:
        return []
    path = []
    current = goal
    while current is not None:
        path.append(current)
        current = predecessors[current]
    return path[::-1]
```

```python
import heapq

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    pq = []
    heapq.heappush(pq, (start[0] + start[1], start[0], start[1]))
    visited = set([start])
    predecessors = {}
    
    while pq:
        _, row, col = heapq.heappop(pq)
        current = (row, col)
        
        if current == goal:
            path = []
            while current != start:
                path.append(current)
                current = predecessors[current]
            path.append(start)
            return path[::-1]
        
        for dr, dc in directions:
            new_row, new_col = row + dr, col + dc
            new_pos = (new_row, new_col)
            if (0 <= new_row < len(grid) and 0 <= new_col < len(grid[0]) and
                grid[new_row][new_col] == '.' and new_pos not in visited):
                visited.add(new_pos)
                predecessors[new_pos] = (row, col)
                heapq.heappush(pq, (new_row + new_col, new_row, new_col))
    
    return []
```
